title: Roman numerals
examples: Teacher, can you show me how to write the number twenty?
What is the biggest number we can write with these letters?
If I see XL, what number is that?

explain.say: Today we learn about Roman numerals. These are old ways to write numbers. We use letters like I, V, X, L, C, D, and M.

items: I, V, X, L, C, D, M

draw.text: I, V, X, L, C, D, M

explain.say: The letters stand for certain values. I is one. V is five. X is ten. These are the basic building blocks you need to know.
Sometimes we subtract. If we see IV, it means five minus one. So IV is four. Remember this pattern for subtraction.
We can use these to write years too. For example, the year nineteen ninety means MCMX. This uses the larger letters.

faq.q: What is the smallest number I can write using Roman numerals?
faq.a: The smallest number is one. You just use the letter I for that value.
asks: What is the value of I?
How do I write the number one?

faq.q: When do I use the subtractive rule?
faq.a: You use subtraction when a smaller value letter comes right before a larger value letter. Like in IV.
asks: When is subtraction used in Roman numerals?

faq.q: What does L stand for in Roman numerals?
faq.a: L stands for the number fifty. It is a key value to remember when counting up.
asks: Can you tell me the value of L?

faq.q: Can I write a very big number like one thousand?
faq.a: Yes, you use the letter M for one thousand. This is one of the largest basic symbols.

faq.q: Do I have to use all the letters I, V, X, L, C, D, M?
faq.a: No, you only use the letters that match the number you are trying to write. You do not need all of them.
asks: Do I use all the symbols?
Which letters do I need for a small number?

facts: M represents the number one thousand.
Subtractive pairs include IV for four and IX for nine.

quiz.say: What number does the Roman numeral XII represent?
quiz.why: You add the values of X and two I's, which is ten plus two.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you might forget to count the second I.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you treat the letters as separate items to be added.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you might think the two I's should be added to the X.

quiz.say: Which Roman numeral correctly shows the number nineteen?
quiz.why: You write ten (X) and then nine (IX) together, which is ten plus nine.

wrong.0: This mistake incorrectly adds two tens instead of using the subtractive rule for nine.
wrong.1: This mistake adds an extra letter that does not belong to the number nineteen.
wrong.3: This mistake adds an extra I, making the number too large.

quiz.say: If you see XL, what number is it?
quiz.why: Because X is ten and L is fifty, the smaller letter X comes before the larger letter L, so you subtract.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you only look at the first two letters and forget the magnitude of L.
wrong.1: This mistake happens because you might confuse the letters with a different Roman numeral pattern.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you incorrectly add the values of X and L together.
